purpose: Coverage inventory, not a pass report or unchanged-upstream execution claim. Every function in these five locked suites is classified; 198 reference parameter cases are not 198 candidate passes. Private Python helpers, backend variants, open metadata gaps and BSON/client/diagnostic/configuration differences are explicit.

Nonfinite BSON values and exact Decimal128 representations beyond Int64 do not match. Arbitrary Python integers outside BSON Int64 cannot travel over the wire and are rejected before mutation, not stored as Python-only values.

This monkeypatches TinyMongo's private Python numeric conversion to raise ArithmeticError. BriskDB has no such helper or hook; typed-BSON nonfinite/out-of-range matching is tested instead. This is not an unchanged injected-branch pass.
Private normalized frozenset identity is replaced by public alias/code-deduplicated matching outcomes.
Decimal BSON query types are checked over the wire. A private helper's classification of an arbitrary Python object is not representable in BSON; the stock driver rejects it before mutation.

This tests identity of a caller-owned arbitrary Python default object in a private helper. No corresponding native/wire API exists; public missing/null/path behavior remains tested, not waived.

Recursive user documents/datetimes are checked across read/write result surfaces. Full listDatabases statistics still fail explicitly with code 115 under #166; only nameOnly metadata is currently available. PyMongo index metadata uses a cursor of SON documents rather than TinyMongo's indexed list of plain dictionaries. TinyMongo's five backend variants are reference coverage only; the candidate uses BriskDB's own two-shard SQLite engine, not those backends.

The same persisted BSON milliseconds are decoded with independent UTC/custom-timezone client options after reopen. TinyMongo's five backend variants are reference coverage only; the candidate uses BriskDB's own two-shard SQLite engine, not those backends.

Submillisecond input changes normalize to identical BSON milliseconds, leaving update/replace modified counts zero. TinyMongo's five backend variants are reference coverage only; the candidate uses BriskDB's own two-shard SQLite engine, not those backends.

UserDict/OrderedDict materialize recursively through separate clients; mutating a returned object cannot mutate stored data or another client's result. TinyMongo's five backend variants are reference coverage only; the candidate uses BriskDB's own two-shard SQLite engine, not those backends.

Both parameterized dict and UserDict aliases materialize root/nested documents as their origin types. TinyMongo's five backend variants are reference coverage only; the candidate uses BriskDB's own two-shard SQLite engine, not those backends.

SON materialization is checked recursively with BSON available, not skipped. TinyMongo's five backend variants are reference coverage only; the candidate uses BriskDB's own two-shard SQLite engine, not those backends.

Real async PyMongo find/clone/to_list/aggregate/distinct/find-and-modify preserve recursive OrderedDict and aware datetimes. TinyMongo's five backend variants are reference coverage only; the candidate uses BriskDB's own two-shard SQLite engine, not those backends.

Ordering, counts, input indices and caller-owned op objects are checked. BriskDB deliberately keeps server diagnostics payload-free: keyPattern/keyValue and interpolated index/key errmsg values are absent, not fabricated. Five reference backends do not imply five BriskDB backends.
Real installed-wheel wire traffic checks accepted IDs, rejected input indices and original operation identity, including mixed ID/secondary-key/missing-key conflicts.

The local helper checks serialization before any insert even beyond 1,000 documents, with ordered/unordered and validation-bypass variants. Generated input IDs survive rejection and no namespace is created. Driver InvalidDocument text is retained, not TinyMongo's custom collection/index/path message format; no transaction or storage-error atomicity is promised.
The actual async PyMongo client shares eager preflight, return IDs, partial duplicate counts and input error indices.
Empty/non-document input, nonboolean ordered and a late failing iterator are rejected before mutation. Empty generators are also rejected explicitly.

Tuple/generator and UserDict input preserves caller IDs, embedded boolean/number identity, explicit null uniqueness, result objects and records across reopen. Caller RawBSONDocument IDs keep stock PyMongo's omission from inserted_ids.
Public scalar-ID update/delete does not target an array-ID record; BriskDB does not share TinyDB's physical storage implementation.
The wire normalizes tuples and lists to the same BSON array identity; the second insert is a duplicate and the first survives.

Excluded private implementation assertions: monkeypatched Python backend find/commit/physical-key functions, fabricated racing engines and exact retry/encoding call counts are not BriskDB APIs. Linked real-wire tests cover public duplicate/counter/identity/concurrency results and client custom encoders once, not the reference's private retry count or native storage optimization.

TinyMongo's fallback errors module when PyMongo is absent is not applicable to the opt-in BriskDB client, which explicitly requires pinned PyMongo. The real PyMongo BulkWriteError shape is exercised; no fallback class is shipped.

TinyMongo's private dynamic/fallback validator-name catalog and monkeypatches do not apply. BriskDB delegates validation to its required pinned PyMongo constructor; it does not publish that helper or a no-PyMongo replacement. Public rejection before storage is checked for both real clients.

The public tinymongo_folder alias is accepted by BriskDB's MongoClient/AsyncMongoClient and persists in that folder. BriskDB stores its own manifest/shards, not TinyDB app.json files, and does not expose TinyMongo private _foldername state or its separate TinyMongoClient classes.

BriskDB requires a single folder option even when aliases have equal values; conflicting aliases also reject. TinyMongo-only threads/duckdb_config and foreign backends are rejected, not silently accepted or advertised as BriskDB backend implementations.
The real async default client constructs and closes; BRISKDB_HOME is isolated to a temporary test root so the test cannot create user data.

Both real client constructors reject malformed document/timezone/unknown options before native acquisition. New roots stay absent and existing stores are not opened or recovered; additional cross-pool validation is covered.
All source falsey document classes and timezone input forms are checked in both sync and async clients with the driver's actual codec settings.
Unknown options fail eagerly as PyMongo ConfigurationError for the public BriskDB clients; TinyMongo's separate TinyMongoClient TypeError class/message is not emulated.

Retained timeout, pool, retry, appName, listener, selector and server_api options use real PyMongo validation. Remote hosts/credentials are deliberately replaced by the owned local endpoint; construction and actual database traffic verify the binding.
